item.title: GitHub Actions
item.description:
GitHub Actions is how Layer5 Cloud meets your pull-request workflow. The Kanvas Snapshot action renders the infrastructure file in a pull request as a Kanvas design and posts the picture as a comment, so reviewers see the resources and their connections before they read the YAML. It runs on GitHub-hosted runners and never touches your cluster.

The action reference, including inputs, the workflow the wizard installs, token handling, and troubleshooting, lives in one place: Kanvas Snapshot.

item.title: Integrations
item.description:
Integrations connect Layer5 Cloud to systems outside it. Today that means GitHub, for importing infrastructure files and posting pull-request snapshots, and the infrastructure connections that Meshery Servers register.

Integration matrix 🔗

Integration What it does Where to start
GitHub (Layer5 GitHub App) Reads the repositories you grant, imports Kubernetes manifests, Helm charts, Docker Compose files, and Meshery designs as private designs, and can commit a snapshot workflow to a repository. Integrating GitHub with Meshery
GitHub Actions (Kanvas Snapshot) Posts a picture of your infrastructure on every pull request. GitHub Actions
Meshery Server Registers each Meshery Server as a connection. Listed under Meshery on the Integrations tab.
Kubernetes Lists the clusters your Meshery Servers manage, so you can assign them to environments. Managing Environments
Prometheus Lists Prometheus connections that Meshery Servers report. Listed under Prometheus on the Integrations tab.

Meshery Servers register Meshery, Kubernetes, and Prometheus connections. Layer5 Cloud has no setup wizard for them. The Integrations tab shows what the servers in your organization registered, and you assign those connections to environments to decide which teams can read them.
